title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections
description: Unlearning concerns the task of removing the influence of a sensitive portion of the training data, such as protected, copyrighted or private text, from a model without retraining it from scratch. While unlearning requests happen continuously during a model's lifetime, the vast majority of LLM unlearning methods are ill-suited for iterated removal, yielding steep decay in forgetting and utility upon sequential unlearning. This decay stems from interference between successive updates, as each new deletion can undo earlier ones or push the model further along directions already degraded by them. To address this, we introduce Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP), a gradient-projection scheme that restricts each update to the orthogonal complement of activation subspaces cached from prior forget sets. This approach provably guarantees first-order non-interference with earlier deletions. COP stores only a low-rank basis per layer, requiring neither past gradients nor previous forget sets, and plugs into unlearning methods that update the model through gradient steps on a differentiable loss without modifying its objective. Experiments on standard LLM unlearning benchmarks (TOFU and RWKU) show that COP preserves utility across sequential requests without weakening forgetting, preventing the collapse of standard objectives and forgetting more effectively than continual-specific baselines.
author: Juan Belieni, Ana Carolina Erthal, Eliezer de Souza da Silva, Diego Mesquita

title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
description: In psychiatric practice, the clinical intake interview remains a primary diagnostic instrument, requiring the clinician to establish rapport while disentangling complex, overlapping presentations. Here, we show that multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation environments improves language model performance on structured text-based psychiatric intake, spanning history-taking, differential diagnosis, and initial management planning. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study ($N = 60$ matched scenario pairs, 120 encounters) comparing the RL-trained agent against its identically prompted base model, 32 board-certified psychiatrists role-played standardized patients while a separate panel of 15 independent, board-certified psychiatrists scored the de-identified transcripts. The trained agent outperformed the base model in 76.7% of matched scenario pairs ($p < 0.0001$), with gains on an adapted clinical-examination rubric ($d_z = 0.77$, $p < 0.0001$), patient-centered communication (82.0% vs. 65.2%, $p < 0.001$), and differential diagnosis appropriateness (68.3% vs. 33.3%, $p < 0.001$). Across 127 psychiatrist-validated simulated intake scenarios, the trained agent nearly doubled its base model's clinical rubric score (0.706 vs. 0.379; composite reward 0.564 vs. 0.294, $p < 0.0001$). title: Flatever - Flat illustration style [LORA/Krea 2]
description:
This LoRA was trained to produce flat-design images. The idea is to use as few lines as possible while keeping the visual clear, relying on solid blocks of color.

While the base model can already generate this style, I made an artistic choice that sets it apart from standard flat design. This choice also introduced a few biases, which may be corrected in the future if I feel like it.

For prompting, in addition to the trigger word, I suggest mentioning the colors and specifying a 2D, flat look to help avoid overly realistic and detailed generations. I hope you have fun with this model—it should be interesting to blend with some of your other favorite LoRAs. The example images were deliberately generated with the base model, but results may sometimes be better with less realistic, smoother models. Anyway, enjoy!

The lora was trained with 99 images 1536x1536 with the Civitai Anima trainer at it's default settings.

Trigger Word: nullpop_style is the main trigger word for this style.
